saints.name: Sts. John and Paul
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: Two brothers of Rome, martyred under Julian the Apostate, whose names are spoken in the Canon of the Mass…
biography: According to their ancient acts, John and Paul were brothers who served in the household of Constantia, daughter of Constantine, and were put to death in their own house on the Caelian Hill under the Emperor Julian the Apostate, about 362, for refusing to worship the gods.
A basilica was raised over their house, which still stands, and their names were placed in the Canon of the Mass, where they are still invoked among the martyrs.
saints.knownFor: Their martyrdom under Julian; named in the Roman Canon.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
